RE: Appeal of Adverse Benefit Determination
Member: Quinn Novak
Member ID: W666121456
Reference Number: POC-638643858B-53234
Date of Notice: 2026-08-23
Service Denied: Total knee replacement, CPT 27447
Requesting/Treating Surgeon: Reyes, MD, Orthopedic Surgery

To the Appeals Review Committee:

I am writing to appeal the denial of prior authorization for total knee arthroplasty (CPT 27447), as set forth in the Notice of Adverse Benefit Determination dated 2026-08-23. This appeal is timely; the notice states that an appeal must be received by 2027-02-19. [Note: TennCare's general appeal rule, Tenn. Comp. R. & Regs. 1200-13-13-.11(2)(d), states enrollees are allowed "sixty (60) days from the date on the written notice ... to appeal any adverse benefit determination." Because this is shorter than the 180-day deadline stated in the notice, I am filing this appeal now, well within either timeframe, and I ask the plan to confirm in writing which deadline governs.]

Stated Reason for Denial

The notice states: "the clinical records submitted do not document an adequate trial of conservative treatment prior to the requested surgery."

I dispute this determination. The medical record submitted with the prior authorization request in fact documents an extensive and adequate trial of conservative treatment, as summarized below.

Response to the Stated Denial Reason, Mapped to the Clinical Record

1. Duration and severity of symptoms: The record documents 12 months of progressive knee pain that has not been relieved by rest, with the patient now unable to climb stairs without assistance and waking 3-4 times nightly due to pain.

2. Supervised physical therapy: The patient completed 16 weeks of supervised physical therapy (2026-03-15 through 2026-07-05), totaling 16 visits, focused on quadriceps strengthening and range-of-motion, as documented in the physical therapy discharge note.

3. Medication trial: The patient completed a 6-month trial of NSAIDs with inadequate relief.

4. Injection therapy: The patient received a corticosteroid injection on 2026-06-04, which produced only 2 weeks of partial relief before symptoms returned.

5. Objective imaging findings: Weight-bearing radiographs obtained 2026-07-01 show bone-on-bone apposition in the medial and patellofemoral compartments with lateral joint-space narrowing, consistent with Kellgren-Lawrence grade 4 disease — the most severe radiographic classification of osteoarthritis.

6. Physical examination findings: Exam documents varus alignment, crepitus, effusion, and a markedly reduced range of motion of 5-100 degrees.

7. Absence of contraindications: The record documents no active infection, no untreated substance use, a BMI of 29, and non-smoker status, none of which present a barrier to surgery.

Taken together, this record documents a supervised, multi-modality conservative treatment trial — physical therapy, sustained NSAID use, and injection therapy — sustained over a period of six to twelve months, that has failed to relieve the patient's pain or restore function, in the setting of radiographically confirmed end-stage (Kellgren-Lawrence grade 4) osteoarthritis. I am not aware of, and the notice does not identify, any specific plan medical policy, clinical guideline, or criteria document defining what "adequate trial of conservative treatment" requires for CPT 27447, or specifying what, if anything, this record is missing. I therefore cannot address a specific policy citation, because none was provided to the patient or the surgeon.

Request for the Specific Medical Necessity Criteria Applied

Please provide, in writing, the specific medical policy, clinical guideline, or utilization-management criteria document (including its title, policy number, and effective date) that was applied to deny this request, along with the specific provision(s) of that document that the submitted record allegedly fails to satisfy. [I understand plans are required to identify the specific rule, guideline, or protocol relied upon in making an adverse benefit determination and to make that guidance available upon request.]

Regulatory Standard Governing This Appeal

I also ask the reviewer to apply the following standards, which govern TennCare adverse benefit determinations under Tenn. Comp. R. & Regs. Ch. 1200-13-13 and 1200-13-16:

- "Neither the TennCare program nor its MCCs may employ utilization control guidelines or other quantitative coverage limits, whether explicit or de facto, unless supported by an individualized determination of medical necessity based upon the needs of each TennCare enrollee and his or her medical history." (Tenn. Comp. R. & Regs. 1200-13-13-.11(3)(a))

- "Medical opinions shall be evaluated pursuant to TennCare Medical Necessity rule 1200-13-16. Reliance upon insurance industry guidelines or utilization control criteria of general application, without consideration of the individual enrollee's medical history, does not satisfy this requirement and cannot be relied upon to support an adverse benefit determination." (Tenn. Comp. R. & Regs. 1200-13-13-.11(3)(b)2)

- Tenn. Comp. R. & Regs. 1200-13-16-.01(1) defines "ADEQUATE," when applied to a medical item or service, to mean that "the item or service, considered as part of a course of diagnosis or treatment, is sufficient, but not in excess of what is needed, for diagnosis or treatment of the particular medical condition."

Applying that definition, the conservative treatment already provided to this patient — 16 weeks of supervised physical therapy, 6 months of NSAID therapy, and a corticosteroid injection — was sufficient to diagnose and attempt to treat the patient's condition short of surgery, and any further delay would not add diagnostic or therapeutic value given the patient's radiographically confirmed Kellgren-Lawrence grade 4 disease and ongoing functional decline. I ask that this individualized clinical picture, rather than a generic conservative-care checklist, be the basis for the medical necessity determination on appeal, consistent with the rules cited above.

Requested Action

I ask that the plan reverse the denial and authorize CPT 27447 (total knee replacement) as requested by Dr. Reyes. In the alternative, I ask that the plan identify, in writing, the specific medical necessity criteria applied and the specific deficiency in the submitted record, so that the treating surgeon may respond directly to that citation.

Enclosures

- Physical therapy discharge note (2026-03-15 to 2026-07-05, 16 visits)
- Medication/injection records (NSAID trial; corticosteroid injection 2026-06-04)
- Weight-bearing knee radiograph report, 2026-07-01
- Physical examination/clinic notes documenting range of motion, alignment, and functional limitations
- [Letter of medical necessity from Dr. Reyes, if available]
- Copy of the Notice of Adverse Benefit Determination dated 2026-08-23

Please confirm receipt of this appeal in writing and provide notice of the outcome as required under TennCare's appeal rules. If any additional information is needed, please contact [patient phone number] or [surgeon's office contact/NPI].

Sincerely,

Quinn Novak
Member ID: W666121456
